title: Acceptance of Supplications in Islam
summary: Certain people's supplications are always accepted, including those fasting at iftar.
translation: The connection between fasting and supplication is profound, as emphasized in a hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He said, 'Three types of people's supplications are not rejected: the fasting person at the time of breaking the fast, the just ruler, and the oppressed person.' This hadith highlights the promise of the acceptance of supplications at iftar for those fasting. Additionally, fasting individuals are bestowed with the grace of angels and sea fish praying for their forgiveness. Therefore, during these blessed moments, when supplicating for one's own forgiveness, family, and relatives, one should also remember the entire Muslim Ummah, praying for the removal of their sorrows and the return of their honor and happiness. May Allah accept all our supplications.
